e. Animal Life
Animal life in its natural sense does not exist within the project and will not be impacted by any phase of the planned program, as can best be determined. No ill effects on migratory animals or animals in the river or surrounding areas are anticipated. Animals that now exist within the area, i. e., birds, squirrels and other members of the rodent family, that have developed an ability to adapt to urbanization, will not be effected by further urbanization for the project area. In some respects, the environment for these creatures will be improved (in the case of birds and squirrels) by the additional trees, new open areas, and planned population redistribution.
f. Vegetation
Vegetation within the area will be improved as a result of the public improvements (additional trees) and the landscaping associated with new development and rehabilitation of private homes and yards; however, this improvement may only be considered nominal given the relative size of the project area and the limited extent of the activity anticipated. No trees in the ares will be needlessly removed. Storm damaged trees will be replaced with new trees.
Interim uses of cleared lots, as indicated in the proposed plan, will be planted and maintained as a project activity during the execution period. Code enforcement activities will tend to improve yard areas and; therefore, the quality of vegetation within the area will be improved.
The public improvements to areas associated with backyards (new pedestrian walkway and lighting) will also tend to create sympathetic improvement of backyard areas (qualitively).
The only negative impact that can be imagined is the accidental damage to trees during demolition, street repair, rehabilitation and new construction. Major damage to trees would be repaired by the party or parties responsible (City or private contractor).
